goal: Fixes a security hole where bitcoind silently falls back to IPv6-only RPC binding if the default IPv4 port is taken, letting a local attacker on another user account steal RPC credentials via a rogue listener.
Restores fail-closed behavior: default IPv4 bind must succeed, and explicit -rpcbind entries must all succeed.
reviewability: Ready. Author actively pushing fixes for nits and the IPv6-only error-message suggestion, no open blocking issues.
agreement: Strong support from multiple reviewers with concept ACKs and no objections (l0rinc, janb84, sedited, winterrdog).
Only nitpicks raised, most already addressed by the author in later pushes.

result.summary: This PR restores fail-closed behavior for the HTTP/RPC server: by default the IPv4 bind must succeed (IPv6 becomes optional), and when -rpcbind is explicitly specified, all listed binds must succeed. It fixes a credential-exfiltration issue where a rogue process squatting on the default IPv4 RPC port could receive bitcoin-cli's plaintext cookie credentials while bitcoind silently continued on IPv6 only. It adds a functional test that captures and verifies the leaked Authorization header scenario, and improves bind failure/error logging.
result.problem: When another process occupies the default IPv4 RPC port, bitcoind currently starts anyway on IPv6, and bitcoin-cli (which defaults to IPv4) sends RPC credentials to that other process in plaintext, allowing a local attacker on a different user account to hijack RPC access. This regressed prior fail-closed behavior from 2012 (referenced PR #1822) and was previously attempted to be fixed in #14968 in 2018 but abandoned due to CI issues.

categories.evidence: Directly modifies src/httpserver.cpp bind logic and error handling for the RPC HTTP server, and adds functional tests in test/functional/rpc_bind.py. Labeled RPC/REST/ZMQ.
categories.rationale: P1 because this closes a credential-exfiltration vector: a rogue local process on a different user account can steal RPC cookie credentials sent in plaintext when bitcoind silently falls back to IPv6-only binding, per the PR description's severity analysis and the new test that captures the leaked Authorization header. This restores intentional 2012 fail-closed behavior (referenced PR #1822) that regressed over time, and revives a previously abandoned 2018 fix attempt (#14968) now made possible by better socket-level bind reporting.the attack requires local multi-user access, which is a real but narrower threat model, keeping this from being an even higher-severity remote issue, but it is still a genuine security defect within the RPC/HTTP server's default configuration.

result.card: This PR restores fail-closed behavior for bitcoind's HTTP/RPC server so that the default IPv4 bind must succeed, closing a credential-exfiltration hole where a local attacker on another user account could squat on the default IPv4 RPC port and receive bitcoin-cli's plaintext cookie credentials while bitcoind silently continued on IPv6 alone. The PR description explains the severity clearly and includes a new functional test that actually captures the leaked Authorization header to prove the vulnerability and the fix. It revives a 2018 attempt (#14968) that was abandoned due to CI issues with IPv6 support, now made feasible because the in-tree socket implementation reports each bind result individually. Four members gave concept ACKs (l0rinc, janb84, sedited, winterrdog) with no objections, only style nits and a suggestion to make the IPv6-only host error message clearer, which the author is actively incorporating via force-pushes. The PR is in a labeled RPC/REST/ZMQ area and is ready for review now, with the author actively engaged as of 2026-09-11.
